newsitem.title: THAILAND: Daiwa says Thai turmoil stalling agreement.
newsitem.headline: Daiwa says Thai turmoil stalling agreement.

text.p: Turbulent conditions in the Thai finance sector are delaying Daiwa Securities's plans to sign agreements with Thai brokers, Chief Representative Officer Yoshihiro Hasegawa said.
The company's local office has been in talks with two Thai firms wishing to sign brokerage deals but instability in the sector has delayed developments, he told Reuters in a telephone interview.

"I'm just picking who the candidates will be for a brokerage agreement and we have narrowed it down to two ... but I think my position at the moment is wait and see to find out what is going on," he said.
Many of Thailand's 91 finance and securities firms are facing a liquidity crunch brought about by a more than 50 percent slump in the Thai stock market over the last 12 months.
Finance firms have been hit by deteriorating loan portfolio quality caused by slowing economic growth and exposure to the troubled Thai property sector.
Last Monday the central bank took the unprecedented step of suspending all finance and bank stocks while identifying 10 ailing firms, and announcing stringent new provisioning measures.

"As you know it is difficult now to take action ... Many local brokers come to see me, to see what I'm thinking or to ask me to give them orders but in this situation I cannot make a big commitment," Hosegawa said.
With the finance sector's frailties expected to lead to the merger of some Thai firms, the risks of an early agreement being wrecked by a merger were prohibitive, Hosegawa said.
"If we put in money to a specific finance and securities company and after that they are merged we will lose ownwership, or it will be diluted, so I'm not sure when it will be," he said.
"Yes hopefully we are looking for control of a securities operation ... I can't say how much (of a stake) we want but I can say I don't want one, three or four percent," he said.
Traders said Daiwa's market share of orders was currently less than one percent of total amerket trade.
A majority of Daiwa's orders currently go through Securities One, but Union Securities and Thanapol Securities also receive orders, dealers said.
